paragraphs: At the beginning of [Jerusalem Talmud Taanit chapter 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Taanit.4.1.4), he was a priest with a crooked finger, and he asked Rabbi Mana II whether he could ascend the platform to give the priestly blessing. There is also Rav Yitzchak bar Naftali in [Ketubot 96a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.96a.11).[^1][^2]

notes.text: Mana II preserves the source’s ב׳. The text records Naftali’s question, not its answer. The separate Yitzchak bar Naftali is not automatically identified as his son.

In the linked Taanit passage, Rabbi Mana permits Naftali to give the blessing because he is known in his town. [Heilprin’s Naftali entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2727&lang=en) also cites the question. The linked Ketubot names Rav Yitzchak bar Naftali speaking to Ravina in Rava’s name, and [Heilprin’s Yitzchak entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2218&lang=en) cites that same passage. These notices do not establish that the two were father and son.
